_comment: Bought parts. 'published' values are quoted from the maker's page at 'source'. 'assumed' values are not published by the maker; each carries the reason it was chosen. Lengths in mm, masses in g.

height_is_case_only.why: the page gives one height; taken as the case without the output spline

shaft_from_end_mm.why: half the case width, as on standard-size servos; not published

ear_overhang_mm.why: typical mounting ear of a standard-size servo; not published

ear_bottom_height_mm.why: about 0.68 of the case height; not published

horn_radius_mm.why: round horn of about 21 mm; the kit's horn is not dimensioned by the maker

horn_face_above_case_mm.why: case top to the outer face of the horn, where the printed blank sits; not published

stall_current_a.why: the maker publishes no stall current; typical for an analog servo of this torque at 5 V

armature_kgm2.why: reflected rotor inertia for the simulation; not published

height_is_case_only.why: the page gives one height; taken as the case without the output spline

shaft_from_end_mm.why: half the case width; not published

ear_overhang_mm.why: typical mounting ear of a mini servo; not published

ear_bottom_height_mm.why: about 0.68 of the case height; not published

horn_radius_mm.why: round horn of about 18 mm; not dimensioned by the maker

horn_face_above_case_mm.why: case top to the outer face of the horn; not published

stall_current_a.why: the maker publishes no stall current; typical for a mini analog servo at 5 V

armature_kgm2.why: reflected rotor inertia for the simulation; not published

supply.note: The Braccio shield feeds the servos from the kit's regulated 5 V supply. The maker rates the servos at 4.8 V and 6.0 V only, so the 4.8 V torque and speed are used.

pcb_thickness_mm.why: standard board thickness; not in the datasheet text

mass_g.why: the datasheet gives no mass; estimate for a populated UNO-format board

spacer_mm.why: insulating spacers the design README asks for; must exceed the 2 mm bottom-side parts

mass_g.why: not published; estimate for the shield with headers and jack

pcb_gap_mm.why: stacking header pitch between board and shield; not published

stack_height_mm.why: top of the servo plugs above the UNO Q board top; not published

esp32cam.name: AI-Thinker ESP32-CAM
esp32cam.source_note: AI-Thinker 'ESP32-CAM Wi-Fi+BT SoC Module V1.0' specification, read from a mirror; docs.ai-thinker.com did not serve the page.

published.connector: none; 2 x 8 pin headers (5V, GND, U0R, U0T, IO0 for power and flashing)

lens_fov_deg.note: 65 to 68 degrees is quoted for the stock OV2640 module; no source says whether diagonal or horizontal

pcb_thickness_mm.why: not published; the snap lips are spaced for 1.6 mm plus 0.3 mm, a thinner board sits loose by the difference

lens_centre_above_lower_edge_mm.why: the camera lies over the card slot at the antenna end, about 9 mm from that edge; not dimensioned by the maker, tolerance 3 mm

lens_front_above_board_mm.why: OV2640 module height on the card slot; not published, tolerance 1.5 mm

lens_diameter_mm.why: module body about 8 mm square; not published

esp_eye.name: Espressif ESP-EYE V2.1
esp_eye.source_note: Espressif's guide names the parts (OV2640 camera, Micro-USB, BOOT and RST buttons on the camera face, a side function button, microphone, 3D antenna) and gives no dimensions. Positions were scaled from its annotated photograph esp-eye_callout.png.

published.connector: Micro-USB on the back face at the short edge away from the camera; powers the board. Mounted upward here.
published.mounting_hole_note: one hole of about 2.3 mm in a corner at the antenna end; one hole cannot locate the board, so it is held by its edges

lens_fov_deg.note: Espressif's figure for the OV2640 on the ESP32-S3-EYE; none is given for the ESP-EYE

lens_centre_above_lower_edge_mm.why: scaled from Espressif's photograph: 9 mm from the camera end, centred; tolerance 1 mm

lens_diameter_mm.why: module body about 7.7 mm square in the photograph

boot_and_reset_above_lower_edge_mm.why: scaled from the photograph: on the camera face, 1.6 mm from each long edge; tolerance 1 mm

side_button_above_lower_edge_mm.why: scaled from the photograph: 29.5 to 34 mm, on the long edge at the robot's left as mounted; tolerance 1 mm

microphone_above_lower_edge_mm.why: scaled from the photograph: camera face, centred, at the USB end

picture_is_upright_with_usb_down.why: the board's lettering reads upright with the connector down; taken as the sensor's upright, not confirmed on a board

esp_eye.mounting_note: Mounted with the Micro-USB connector up and the camera end down, so nothing has to be kept clear under the board. Heights below are from the lower edge as mounted, which is the camera and antenna end. The picture is then upside down: set VFLIP and HMIRROR to 1 in the sketchbot's esp_eye_camera sketch.

esp32_s3_eye.name: Espressif ESP32-S3-EYE v2.2
esp32_s3_eye.source_note: Espressif's dimension drawings of the main board and its getting-started guide (https://github.com/espressif/esp-who/blob/master/docs/en/get-started/ESP32-S3-EYE_Getting_Started_Guide.md).

published.mounting_hole_note: two holes of about 3 mm in the corners at the antenna end; not used, the antenna end is left open
published.connector: Micro-USB on the back face at the lower short edge

mass_g.why: not published; estimate with the LCD sub board, tolerance 8 g

lens_centre_above_lower_edge_mm.why: scaled from the drawing: 10.6 mm from the antenna end, centred; tolerance 0.5 mm

lens_diameter_mm.why: module body scaled from the drawing

stack_thickness.why: the drawings are flat; where the LCD sub board's headers sit along the long edges is not known, so the lip and ledge positions of this preset are the least certain of the three

clear_cone_half_angle_deg.why: covers 66.5 degrees whether that figure is the diagonal or the horizontal field of a 4:3 sensor (39.3 degrees to the corner in the second case)

material.why: the design README names no material

density_g_cm3.why: typical PLA filament data sheet value; PETG is about 1.27

solid_fraction.why: 4 mm plates with two perimeters and 0.8 mm skins at 20 percent infill are mostly shell

screwdriver_radius_mm.why: shank of a small cross-head driver for the horn screw

screwdriver_length_mm.why: free length needed in front of the access hole

body_length_mm.why: largest of the SG90 data sheet figures; M5Stack gives no body size for the servo alone

body_below_ears_mm.why: largest of the SG90 figures (17 to 19.5)

shaft_from_body_centre_mm.why: typical of the SG90; not on the data sheets read; measure

horn_face_above_deck_top_mm.why: ears on the deck top, gear housing 10 mm, spline and horn about 4.5 mm; measure with the horn or adapter fitted

same_case_for_180_and_360.why: both are named SG90 by M5Stack; not stated

adapter_hole_pattern.value: four holes at 8 mm from the axis
adapter_hole_pattern.why: the kit's LEGO-compatible adapter is not dimensioned by M5Stack; measure with calipers

pixy.name: Charmed Labs Pixy2 and pan-tilt kit

published.pan_tilt_servos_plug_into: the Pixy2's own two servo connectors

pan_tilt_base_slot_spacing_mm.why: the kit's base is not dimensioned by the maker; measure

pan_tilt_base_slot_length_mm.why: allows for the unknown hole spacing; measure

first_pixy_board_mm.why: 2.1 x 2.0 inches as commonly quoted for the first Pixy; not read from Charmed Labs' pages

controllers._comment: Controllers the biped's deck has a torso variant for, other than the UNO Q with the Braccio shield (see 'board' and 'shield'). 'box_mm' is where the analysis puts the controller as one block in the torso frame (min corner, max corner): an assumption of this repository. Masses include what the entry names.

pi_zero_2w.name: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W with a PCA9685 servo driver board

pi_mass_g.why: not in the product brief; estimate

mass_g.why: Pi estimate plus the driver board with headers (9 g, Adafruit)

stack_height_mm.why: Pi, header and driver board above it; not measured

box_mm.why: long side along x on 3 mm bosses, centred on the deck

pi.name: Raspberry Pi, full size, with a PCA9685 servo driver board

length_mm.why: the usual full-size Raspberry Pi outline; not read from a Raspberry Pi drawing in this work

hole_pattern_mm.why: as given for the full-size boards; 3.5 mm in from one short edge; not read from a Raspberry Pi drawing in this work

mass_g.why: about 46 g for a Raspberry Pi 4 plus the 9 g driver; the board mass is not from a maker's page

stack_height_mm.why: board, connectors and driver; not measured

box_mm.why: long side across the robot on 3 mm bosses, so the board clears the camera mount

hub51515.name: LEGO Technic large hub of the Robot Inventor 51515 set, with its battery

same_as_spike_prime_hub_45601.why: the sheet is for the SPIKE Prime large hub; that the 51515 hub has the same case and mass is taken as known, not sourced

battery_mass_g.why: LEGO's battery sheet gives no mass; estimate, tolerance 30 g

mass_g.why: hub without battery (published) plus the battery estimate

box_mm.why: long side across the robot, resting on the two pad rows and the rear pad

ev3.name: LEGO EV3 Intelligent Brick with six AA cells
ev3.source_note: LEGO's EV3 user guide, read from a third-party host, gives ports and batteries only. No LEGO page read in this work gives the brick's dimensions or mass.

published.power: 6 AA cells or the rechargeable pack

mass_g.why: not found; estimate for the brick with six AA cells, tolerance 60 g

box_mm.why: long side across the robot on the hub torso, as far back as the deck allows; there is no torso made for it

round_display.name: Seeed Studio Round Display for XIAO with a XIAO ESP32S3 in its socket

published.display_outline: 39 mm disc (the product page also lists 43 x 43 mm)
published.xiao_socket: on the back; facing the screen, the XIAO's USB-C points right and the power switch is at the lower left
published.battery_connector: JST 1.25 mm, 2 pin, at the rim under the XIAO's USB-C end
published.charging: 3.7 V lithium cell through the XIAO's USB port, about 485 mA
published.sense_camera: OV2640 discontinued; OV3660 or OV5640 on current stock; module about 8 x 8 mm on a flex about 21 mm long overall

glass_diameter_mm.why: Seeed says 39 mm disc and its photos show the glass slightly larger than the board; measure

rim_thickness_mm.why: glass front to the back of the board at the rim; not published; measure

stack_depth_mm.why: glass front to the back of the XIAO; not published; measure

mass_g.why: display and XIAO together; Seeed publishes neither; tolerance 8 g

camera_faces_away_from_the_screen.why: Seeed's text puts the XIAO on the back and its camera-project pictures show the lens looking out of the back; no sentence says so

mounting.why: three M2 standoffs show on the back in Seeed's picture but their positions are not published

published.note: an example of the size class from another maker; its JST-PH plug does not fit the display's JST 1.25 socket

length_mm.why: the owner's cell is not known; measure
